parts.title: 1 · Resolve the recordings
parts.body: The catalog adapter turns the user's selection (a SoundHub project, a folder, a bucket prefix, a sheet) into an explicit list of recordings.

parts.title: 2 · Submit the list
parts.body: The run manager freezes that list. From here on the run never asks the source again, so the run always means the same recordings.

parts.title: 3 · Check the terms
parts.body: The governance adapter asks whether this use of these recordings is allowed before any work starts.

parts.title: 4 · Record the run
parts.body: The run, its recording list and its tasks go into PostgreSQL. Recordings that already have a current result for the same settings are skipped.

parts.title: 5 · Write the work files
parts.body: One work.json per task goes to storage: which model, which settings, which recordings, and where to write outputs.

parts.title: 6 · Launch the workers
parts.body: The compute adapter starts one job per task, passing the worker image's digest and the path to its work file.

parts.title: 7 · Each worker runs its task
parts.body: Outside the core, with files only and no database. A worker reads its work file, runs the inference engine through the model's adapter, and writes outputs plus one outcome for every recording.

parts.title: 8 · Read the result files
parts.body: The run manager reads each task's result.json from storage and checks it against the work file it wrote.

parts.title: 9 · Record the outcomes
parts.body: In one transaction: the task's outcome, each recording's outcome, and its output files. Valid results become current.

parts.title: 10 · Stamp outputs
parts.body: The governance adapter puts a provenance stamp on every result, with the terms that apply to it.
